transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I can’t stop fixating on how awful I look on camera and in photos, and it’s starting to affect my work and social life. It has just gotten to the point where it's really overwhelming, so a close friend encouraged me to come speak with someone.

When you avoid photos, camera calls, or social situations, is it mainly because you’re afraid other people will judge or notice a flaw in your appearance, or because you feel generally embarrassed or anxious in social settings even when your looks aren’t the focus?

It is definitely about how I look, not a general fear of socializing. I am terrified that people will notice my dark circles and bloated face and judge me for looking exhausted or sloppy, especially after some coworkers made comments about me looking "tired" on screen. If my appearance isn't the focus, I don't feel anxious at all.
Do you think these appearance flaws are definitely obvious and real to other people, or is part of you able to recognize that you may be seeing them as worse than others do?

To me, it feels incredibly real and obvious, and I'm constantly convinced that everyone is judging me for looking exhausted and sloppy. Even though my friends tell me they don't notice anything wrong when I ask them, I still can't stop replaying the images in my head. Because of that, it is really hard for me to believe that I might just be exaggerating it.

Because of these worries about your face, do you find yourself doing things like repeatedly checking mirrors or photos, comparing yourself with others, seeking reassurance, or trying to hide the areas you dislike? If so, which of these do you do most often?

Yes, absolutely. Before any video call or social event, I spend 30 to 40 minutes adjusting the lighting, testing angles, and redoing my makeup to hide my puffy face and eye bags. During the calls, I constantly check my camera preview box, and afterward, I zoom in on tagged photos and repeatedly ask my friends if I looked that bad.

At your deepest level, do you believe these appearance problems are definitely true and obvious to everyone, or can you admit there’s at least a chance your mind may be exaggerating them? Have you ever felt completely certain of it, like no one could convince you otherwise?

To be honest, at my deepest level, it feels completely real and obvious, and there are times when I am absolutely certain no one could convince me otherwise. Even when my friends reassure me that they don't notice anything, I'm convinced they're just being polite to spare my feelings. I just can't shake the belief that everyone else must secretly see how exhausted and sloppy I look.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance (dark circles, bloated/puffy face) that others reportedly do not notice, accompanied by repetitive appearance-related behaviors including mirror/photo checking, reassurance seeking, camouflaging, and prolonged grooming. The concern causes marked social and occupational impairment and is specifically appearance-focused rather than due to generalized social anxiety. Insight is poor to absent/delusional at times, which is consistent with body dysmorphic disorder in ICD-10 category F45.2.
